title: Split-target affinity leak caused stuck promotion and backend saturation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a staged model promotion we observed an unexpected traffic migration that pinned most live requests to the canary variant for ~12 minutes, causing backend GPU pools to saturate and increased 5xx rates for downstream customers. This ticket captures the incident investigation, proposed fixes, and follow-ups.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-04 14:12 UTC: Canary rollout initiated (10% weight) for model v2026-03-01-b.
- 2026-03-04 14:15 UTC: Latency began rising on serving fleet; autoscaler triggered additional warmups.
- 2026-03-04 14:18 UTC: Datadog alerted (internal.alerts.route-anomaly) — canary received ~72% of traffic for some routes.
- 2026-03-04 14:22 UTC: Ops initiated manual mitigation (pin original variant); partial rollback failed due to a version-pin race.
- 2026-03-04 14:34 UTC: Hotfix deployed that forced route-affinity reset; traffic returned to expected split by 14:36 UTC.
- Impact window: ~14 minutes; peak customer 5xx increase +9pp; median latency across affected routes +220ms.

Root cause analysis (concise):
- A new 'split-target-affinity' optimization (merged in runtime-1.22) introduced a default 'sticky=true' behavior for routes with split-targets to reduce KV cache churn. That change toggled route affinity for a subset of routes.
- Simultaneously, the rollout subsystem had a transient race when applying per-route weight updates: the weight delta path applied, but the affinity metadata update (which should have been transactional) failed to commit on one control-plane shard due to an optimistic concurrency check. The result: traffic continued to be sticky to the canary for existing sessions while new requests were weighted, producing an effective >70% percent exposure.
- During this period autoscaling reacted to per-node pressure and produced warmup churn that increased tail latency and 5xx errors while some request paths hit overloaded kernels.

Contributing factors / why safeguards didn't stop it:
- Affinity metadata was stored as a separate keyspace from weights; there was no cross-key transaction/rollforward to guarantee atomicity.
- Rollout canary promotion logic assumes idempotent affinity state; it did not verify post-update affinity convergence before returning success to the API.
- The monitoring rule we relied on (percentage split divergence) had a 5-minute evaluation window and a conservative threshold set for flapping, so it did not fire early enough.

Immediate remediation taken:
- Force-reset affinity metadata for affected routes (hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/3412) and applied a conservative backoff to rollout traffic.
- Applied emergency circuit-breaker to pause new canary promotions until affinity convergence checks pass.
- Notified customers and posted an incident update (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Split-Affinity-Leak-Incident).

Permanent action items (owner / ETA):
- Convert rollout weight + affinity updates to a transactional control-plane operation OR add a two-phase commit fallback. Owner: @Connor Lee. ETA: 2026-03-28.
- Add an affinity-convergence verification step in the rollout API: require observed route affinity to match intended state for at least 60s before marking promotion complete. Owner: @Marta Ruiz. ETA: 2026-04-04.
- Split-target-affinity default should be opt-in in runtime-1.22; revert default and ship as opt-in with explicit experiments. Owner: @Dev Platform. ETA: 2026-03-18.
- Tighten monitoring: add a short-window (30s) anomaly detector for sudden split deviation >15pp. Owner: @Observability SRE. ETA: 2026-03-11. (Hot path implemented as of 2026-03-08).
- Add automated rollback guard to prevent partial-promotions when backend GPU pool utilization >75%. Owner: @Autoscaler team. ETA: 2026-04-08.

Open questions / trade-offs discussed:
- Two-phase commit increases control-plane latency for promotions; we discussed a hybrid approach (fast-path best-effort update + background reconciliation with enforced pause on mismatch). Decision: implement verification + background reconciliation first, then evaluate transactional approach.
- Opt-in for affinity reduces perf wins from the feature; but immediate safety requires opt-in. After verification added, we'll rerun canaries behind stronger monitors.

Related artifacts and dashboards:
- Datadog incident dashboard: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/RW-traffic-split-incident
- Grapher: per-route KV-cache hit/miss: internal link: grapher.redwood/split-affinity-2026-03-04
- Postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Split-Affinity-Leak-Postmortem
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/3412

Acceptance criteria for closure:
- Affinity verification step merged and deployed + two regressions tests (unit + e2e) validating convergence semantics. (PRs linked in comments.)
- Short-window split deviation monitor alerts on synthetic test within 30s.
- Runbook updated with 'affinity-reset' steps and automated remediation playbook.
